details: The European Central Bank's latest Macroprudential Bulletin, published on May 10, 2026, explores the evolving landscape of tokenization and Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) in financial markets. The report highlights both opportunities, such as efficiency gains and enhanced investor access, and inherent vulnerabilities, including secondary market liquidity bottlenecks and platform fragmentation. Notably, the ECB is actively developing infrastructure like its Pontes initiative to integrate DLT-based markets with central bank money settlement, signaling a strategic, long-term engagement with these technologies.
title: ECB Maps Promise & Peril of Tokenized Capital Markets in New Bulletin

details: On May 8, 2026, European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde voiced strong opposition to the use of euro-pegged stablecoins as a means to enhance the euro's international standing. Lagarde argued that private digital tokens are susceptible to vulnerabilities during periods of market stress and could potentially disrupt traditional banking by diverting deposits, thereby complicating the ECB's monetary policy transmission. She advocated for public-sector initiatives, such as a robust safe-asset foundation, as a more sustainable path forward.
title: ECB Chief Lagarde Rejects Euro Stablecoins to Boost Currency Standing
